sentences.text: Adamanasuchus was a relatively large aetosaur characterized by unique armor plating.
The paramedian osteoderms, which are the bony plates running down the back, are narrow, measuring approximately 200 to 225 mm, and arched at about a 30-degree angle.
This animal is known from partial fossil material including dorsal armor, caudal vertebrae, and a femur.
The dorsal armor of Adamanasuchus is distinctive, representing a mosaic of features found in only a few aetosaur genera.
Fossils of Adamanasuchus have been found in the Chinle Group in Arizona.
The locality where Adamanasuchus was named lends its name to the Adamanian land vertebrate faunachron.
Adamanasuchus is classified within the order Aetosauria.
It belongs to the family Stagonolepididae.
The species is placed in the subfamily Desmatosuchinae.
Taxonomically, the genus is classified within the class Sauropsida and is considered a reptile.
The genus Adamanasuchus was originally described anonymously in 1983.
The type species is A. rectori, described anonymously in 1983, while A. eisenhardtae was described by Lucas, Hunt & Spielmann in 2007.
Adamanasuchus lived in the Chinle Formation in present-day Arizona during the Late Triassic period.
The time range for Adamanasuchus is from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago, specifically within the Norian stage.

Adamanasuchus lived contemporaneously with many other aetosaur genera including Longosuchus, Coahomasuchus, Stagonolepis, Desmatosuchus, Tecovasuchus, Paratypothorax, Typothorax, Rioarribasuchus, Aetosaurus, and Redondasuchus.
